_comment: The tests' made-up setting's voice for the player's AI (TestAi): every use the game asks, over the core's
prompts. Made for the tests, not any setting's.
persona: You write for {title}, a game about street racing in a small town.
Write as people there talk: plain, short, a little cocky.
Never mention that this is a game, never explain, never add notes or quotation marks.
Keep every name, car, number and fact you are given exactly as given, and invent none about them.
Write in {language}. Speeds, distances and fuel in {units}.

talk.prompt:
{name} "{nickname}", {age}, a {temper} street racer ({standing}), says this to the player at the diner or from a car window: "{line}"
Say the same thing in {name}'s own voice, one or two short sentences. Answer with the words only.

street_talk.prompt:
A line of gossip overheard at the diner: "{line}"
Tell it again the way a regular at the counter would, one or two sentences, keeping every name and fact. Answer with the words only.

ad.prompt:
A classified ad in the paper offers a {kind}: "{blurb}"
Write the ad's few words again, livelier but as short (at most twelve words), in the clipped style of period classifieds, keeping every fact and adding none: no price, no phone number, nothing the ad does not say. Answer with the words only.

portrait_look.prompt:
Describe for a photographer, in English, how {name} "{nickname}" looks: a {age}-year-old {sex}, a street racer. {biography}
One line of comma-separated visual details: face, hair, expression, clothes, pose. No names, no sentences.

examples.answer: Starts every morning, rain or shine. Don't take my word for it, come take her round the block.
Hot enough to fry an egg on the hood. Now, you calling about the car or the weather?
I'm no good at describing that sort of thing. Come and sit in her, see for yourself.
If it's not on my sheet, I won't promise it, pal. Hop in and have a look while I get the keys.
I'll give it to you straight, pal: everything on the sheet, nothing dressed up. Then you tell me that isn't a deal.

examples.player: I need to think about it.
examples.answer: Sure, sure, think all you want. Just don't think too long: a car like this doesn't sit on my lot for a week.
That's for me to know, man. You'll find out when you're looking at my taillights.
Everybody is. Half the cars there are for show and the other half for go. Guess which one I bring.
Big talk. Bring your car and your money, and we'll see who's laughing.
My kid's turning sixteen, and I'd rather he learn on something solid than something fast.
Maybe to you. I've been reading the paper a while, and I know what they go for.
Today's no good, I'm working. Let's settle the price first and the rest is easy.

examples.player: What've you got that'll make it faster?
examples.answer: Depends what you're running, friend. Tell me the car and I'll tell you what the dyno says.
Best for the money on your engine, yes. The dearer ones look nice on the shelf, but the dyno doesn't lie.

examples.player: Can you knock a few bucks off?
examples.answer: Prices are on the tag, pal. I don't set 'em, I just ring 'em up.

examples.player: This block's tired. What can you do?
examples.answer: Let me mike the bores. If they're not too far gone I'll take it thirty over and fit pistons to suit, and it'll run like new.

examples.player: I want more power out of it.
examples.answer: Then the heads are where it is. Port 'em and polish 'em and she'll breathe, and the dyno will show you.
That's the price of doing it right, friend. Cheap machine work is how engines come back here in pieces.

machinist_search.prompt:
A customer at a machine shop's counter said: "{said}"
The talk before it:
{talk}

Read what work the customer is asking about, as a search of the jobs the shop can do on the parts they brought. Answer with a JSON object only:
- asks: true when they ask about work on their parts (or say which job talked about they mean); false for small talk.
- kind: the kind of part they mean, one of: {kinds}; or "any" when they name none.
- fits: false.
- maxPrice: the most they want to spend, in dollars, as a number; 0 when they name no limit.
- words: a part or a job they named ("heads", "bore", "cam"), as they wrote it; "" when none.
- want: "power" when they want more power or speed, "cheap" when they want it cheap, else "any".
Example: "what would you do to the heads for more power?" gives {"asks": true, "kind": "any", "fits": false, "maxPrice": 0, "words": "head", "want": "power"}.

clerk_search.prompt:
A customer at a part shop's counter said: "{said}"
The talk before it:
{talk}

Read what the customer is asking for, as a search of the shop's stock. Answer with a JSON object only:
- asks: true when they ask for parts or what the shop has (or say which of the parts talked about they mean); false for small talk.
- kind: the kind of part they want, one of: {kinds}; or "any" when they name none.
- fits: true when they want parts for their own car ("for my car", "what fits"), or by default when they ask what would help their car.
- maxPrice: the most they want to spend, in dollars, as a number; 0 when they name no limit.
- words: a make or a part name they named ("Brand X", "V8", "twin carbs"), as they wrote it; "" when none.
- want: "power" when they want more power or speed, "cheap" when they want it cheap, else "any".
Example: "got a cheap carb that fits my Chevy, under 150?" gives {"asks": true, "kind": "Carburetors", "fits": true, "maxPrice": 150, "words": "", "want": "cheap"}.
